Candidate sketch • Unneeded notes are hidden.\nCircled = place; crossed out = remove.
Candidate sketch • Unneeded notes are hidden.\nSolid link: exactly one is true. Dashed: at most one.\nCrossed out = remove.
Only 5 is missing from this row. Put 5 in the circled cell.

string-array.name: lesson_last_digit_steps
string-array.item: Find a row, column, or box with one empty cell.
Identify the missing digit from 1–9.
Fill the empty cell with that digit.

resources.string: In this cell, 1–4 and 6–9 have been ruled out. The only remaining candidate is 5.

string-array.name: lesson_naked_single_steps
string-array.item: Check an empty cell’s possible digits.
Rule out digits already placed in its row, column, or box.
If one candidate remains, place it.

resources.string: 5 appears only in the third cell of this row, even though that cell also has 2 and 9. The rest of the row has no candidate 5.

string-array.name: lesson_hidden_single_steps
string-array.item: Choose one missing digit in a row, column, or box.
Check every empty cell in that unit for the digit.
If it fits in just one cell, place it there—even if that cell has other candidates.

resources.string: In the top-left box, all candidate 5s lie in row 1. Remove 5 from row 1 outside that box.

string-array.name: lesson_pointing_steps
string-array.item: Choose a digit inside one box.
Check whether all its possible cells share one row or column.
Remove that digit from the rest of that line, outside the box.

resources.string: Row 1 has only two places for 5, both in the top-left box. Remove 5 from the other cells of that box.

string-array.name: lesson_claiming_steps
string-array.item: Choose a digit in a row or column.
Check whether all its possible cells fall inside one box.
Remove that digit from the other cells of that box, outside the line.

resources.string: Rows 1 and 5 each have just two places for 5. The candidates in column 2 cannot both be true, so at least one outer end is 5. The crossed-out 5 sees both outer ends.

string-array.name: lesson_skyscraper_steps
string-array.item: Find two rows with exactly two candidates each for the same digit; columns work too.
One pair of ends must align in a column. The other ends are the roofs.
At least one roof must contain the digit. Remove it from any other cell that sees both roofs.

resources.string: Row 1 and column 2 each have just two places for 5. Their inner ends share a box. At least one outer end is 5, so remove 5 at row 7, column 7.

string-array.name: lesson_kite_steps
string-array.item: Find one row and one column with exactly two candidates each for the same digit.
One end from each line must be in the same box, in different cells.
Remove the digit from any other cell that sees both outer ends.

resources.string: The green pivot has {1,2}; its wings have {1,3} and {2,3}. Either pivot choice forces a wing to be 3. Remove 3 where both wings can see it.

string-array.name: lesson_xy_wing_steps
string-array.item: Find a cell with exactly two candidates, X and Y.
Find two cells that see it, with exactly {X,Z} and {Y,Z}.
Remove Z from any other cell that sees both wings. Cells see each other when they share a row, column, or box.

resources.string: The pivot has {1,2,3}; its wings have {1,3} and {2,3}. One of these three cells must be 3. The crossed-out 3 sees the pivot and both wings.

string-array.name: lesson_xyz_wing_steps
string-array.item: Find a pivot with exactly three candidates: X, Y, and Z.
Find two cells that see the pivot, with exactly {X,Z} and {Y,Z}.
Remove Z only from other cells that see all three cells, including the pivot.

resources.string: Both wings have {1,2}. Column 5 has exactly two places for 1, each seeing a different wing. One wing must be 2, so remove 2 where both wings can see it.

string-array.name: lesson_w_wing_steps
string-array.item: Find two cells with the same two candidates, X and Y.
Find a unit with exactly two places for X, each seeing a different wing.
One wing must be Y. Remove Y from any other cell that sees both wings.

resources.string: Follow the solid links on 5, alternating blue and orange. The crossed-out 5 sees blue in its box and orange in its column, so either color rules it out.

string-array.name: lesson_coloring_steps
string-array.item: For one digit, link pairs that are its only two places in a row, column, or box.
Alternate two colors along connected links. One whole color must be true.
Remove an uncolored candidate if it sees both colors.
If two candidates of the same color see each other, that color is false; remove all candidates of that color.

resources.string: Follow the linked 5s from row 1, column 1 to row 4, column 8. The links alternate solid/dashed and end solid. At least one end is 5; the crossed-out 5 sees both.

string-array.name: lesson_x_chain_steps
string-array.item: Use candidates of one digit. A strong link means one must be true; a weak link means they cannot both be true.
Alternate strong and weak links, starting and ending with a strong link.
At least one endpoint is true. Remove the digit from any other cell that sees both endpoints.

resources.string: The chain runs {1,2} → {2,3} → {3,4} → {4,1}. If the first cell is not 1, the last must be 1. Remove 1 from the crossed-out cell, which sees both ends.

string-array.name: lesson_xy_chain_steps
string-array.item: Build a chain of cells that each have exactly two candidates.
Between cells, link matching candidates that see each other; inside each cell, switch to its other candidate.
End on the same digit you started with. Remove it from any other cell that sees both ends.

resources.string: Assume the orange cell is 1. The next cells must be 3, then 4, then 1. That puts two 1s in column 1—a contradiction. Remove the original candidate 1.

string-array.name: lesson_forcing_steps
string-array.item: Temporarily assume one candidate is true.
Follow only forced placements and eliminations. If you branch, check every possibility.
If the assumption inevitably breaks a Sudoku rule or leaves a cell or digit with no place, remove it.
Discard the temporary placements; keep only the proven removal.

resources.string: This row fragment has two highlighted cells containing only 1, 2. Those digits occupy these cells, so the crossed-out 1 is removed from another cell in the row.

string-array.name: lesson_naked_pair_steps
string-array.item: Find two cells in one row, column, or box.
Both cells must have exactly the same two candidates, with no other candidates.
Remove these digits from every other cell in that unit.

resources.string: In this row, 1, 2 occur only in the two highlighted cells. Remove the crossed-out extra notes from those cells; keep 1, 2.

string-array.name: lesson_hidden_pair_steps
string-array.item: Choose two digits in one row, column, or box.
All their candidate positions must fit inside exactly two cells, with no occurrences elsewhere in that unit.
Remove every other candidate from those two cells.

resources.string: This row fragment has three highlighted cells containing only 1, 2, 3. Those digits occupy these cells, so the crossed-out 1 is removed from another cell in the row.

string-array.name: lesson_naked_triple_steps
string-array.item: Find three cells in one row, column, or box.
Together, their candidates must contain exactly three different digits. Each cell can contain fewer than three.
Remove these digits from every other cell in that unit.

resources.string: In this row, 1, 2, 3 occur only in the three highlighted cells. Remove the crossed-out extra notes from those cells; keep 1, 2, 3.

string-array.name: lesson_hidden_triple_steps
string-array.item: Choose three digits in one row, column, or box.
All their candidate positions must fit inside exactly three cells, with no occurrences elsewhere in that unit.
Remove every other candidate from those cells. Each cell need not contain all three chosen digits.

resources.string: This row fragment has four highlighted cells containing only 1, 2, 3, 4. Those digits occupy these cells, so the crossed-out 1 is removed from another cell in the row.

string-array.name: lesson_naked_quad_steps
string-array.item: Find four cells in one row, column, or box.
Together, their candidates must contain exactly four different digits. Each cell can contain fewer than four.
Remove these digits from every other cell in that unit.

resources.string: In this row, 1, 2, 3, 4 occur only in the four highlighted cells. Remove the crossed-out extra notes from those cells; keep 1, 2, 3, 4.

string-array.name: lesson_hidden_quad_steps
string-array.item: Choose four digits in one row, column, or box.
All their candidate positions must fit inside exactly four cells, with no occurrences elsewhere in that unit.
Remove every other candidate from those cells. Each cell need not contain all four chosen digits.

resources.string: In highlighted rows 1 and 4, every candidate 5 is in columns 2 and 5. Those columns must use their 5s in these rows. Remove the crossed-out 5 outside them.

string-array.name: lesson_x_wing_steps
string-array.item: Choose one digit and two rows where it is still missing.
All candidates in those rows must be confined to exactly two columns.
Remove the digit from those columns outside the chosen rows. The same pattern works with rows and columns swapped.

resources.string: In highlighted rows 1, 4, and 7, every candidate 5 is in columns 2, 5, and 8. Those columns must use their 5s in these rows. Remove the crossed-out 5 outside them.

string-array.name: lesson_swordfish_steps
string-array.item: Choose one digit and three rows where it is still missing.
All candidates in those rows must be confined to exactly three columns; each row can use fewer than three of them.
Remove the digit from those columns outside the chosen rows. The same pattern works with rows and columns swapped.

resources.string: In highlighted rows 1, 4, 7, and 9, every candidate 5 is in columns 2, 5, 8, and 9. Those columns must use their 5s in these rows. Remove the crossed-out 5 outside them.

string-array.name: lesson_jellyfish_steps
string-array.item: Choose one digit and four rows where it is still missing.
All candidates in those rows must be confined to exactly four columns; each row can use fewer than four of them.
Remove the digit from those columns outside the chosen rows. The same pattern works with rows and columns swapped.
